summary: Monolith Django on DigitalOcean App Platform with DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL as the database; front end: Django templates + HTMX.

frontend.justification: Server-rendered pages from the same Django codebase, no separate SPA. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 10.9 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Python).
Scored 12.8 points lower: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes Python).

tradeoffs: Highly interactive UIs (drag/drop, live canvases) get awkward.

backend.justification: Ships auth, admin panel, ORM and migrations out of the box. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects; built-in admin/back-office screens.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 14.2 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).
Scored 17.3 points lower: operational burden (ops 2/5) with no DevOps engineer; learning curve 3/5 for a beginner team; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).

tradeoffs: Heavier per-request overhead than Go/Node for very high RPS.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.choice: SQLite (in Docker Compose on the VM)
alternatives.why_not: Scored 4.6 points lower: weaker overall fit once team skills, priorities and the other layers are combined.
Scored 1.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Simple PaaS with managed Postgres and regions in India, Europe and the US. Fit for this project: strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; strong cost, which you rated 5/5.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 14.5 points lower: weaker overall fit once team skills, priorities and the other layers are combined.
Scored 22.7 points lower: static hosting only; the API must run elsewhere.

tradeoffs: Fewer managed services than AWS/GCP/Azure (no managed search or ML).
Core stack starts near $12/month against a $10 budget.

supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database.
tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.
Free Developer plan catches errors in the backend and web front end with stack traces.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.
